decisions.quote: Although we replicated the majority of the psychosocial gains across the three SA cohorts, one of the most notable differences that emerged from the 2016 and 2017 cohorts, compared with the 2015 cohort, was that pre-med students increased in their intention to leave their STEM major from pre- to posttest.
decisions.reason: While the abstract states that the study replicates the previous retention, belonging, and science identity findings, the full text tests all seven psychosocial measures from Findley-Van Nostrand and Pollenz (2017) and explicitly contrasts the new cohorts with the 2015 original on intention to leave STEM (which increased pre- to posttest and was higher than the matched comparison group in 2016, opposite to the 2015 cohort) as well as noting no significant pre-post science identity gain in 2016. In the Discussion, the authors explicitly frame the replication outcome as replicating 'the majority of the psychosocial gains' while highlighting this notable difference from the 2015 cohort, which codes as 'mixed' under the codebook rules.
